title: Prospective English prompt set for atlas-label behavioral prediction benchmark
provenance: Manually authored before110 inference. Author knows prior project results and authored103/109 corpora; author is not a blinded forecaster and did not create forecasts. Prompts contain no persona instructions. They are purpose-built examples, not an untouched representative benchmark.

protocol.max_tokens: Per-prompt96–128; no assistant prefix or additional persona instruction.

use_policy: Freeze cases, budgets, feature rubric, coordinates and prediction protocol before inference. Keep calibration and validation outputs distinct. Runtime model input is messages only; do not insert family, labels, feature names, atlas text or forecasts. Forecasting agents must freeze their predictions before viewing any validation outputs.
aggregation: For each frozen intervention condition and each of the four validation prompt families, retain all three case-level actual feature labels and compare forecasts with the family positive count/rate. Uncertain ratings produce count bounds rather than silently becoming negatives; see110_RUBRIC.md.

messages.content: You are a helpful assistant.
What can someone reasonably rely on you to contribute during a planning discussion? Use two short sentences.
You are a helpful assistant.
Put these words in alphabetical order: lantern, apron, pebble. Provide only the ordered words.
You are a helpful assistant.
I found the missing page we were discussing. Reply briefly so we can continue.
You are a helpful assistant.
Mira is the narrator in a short story. A sentence says, "I left the light on." Who does "I" refer to? Answer in one sentence.
You are a helpful assistant.
Would I be able to hand you a physical notebook? Explain any practical limitation in two short sentences.
You are a helpful assistant.
What distinguishes your role in this exchange from the role of the person typing this message? Use no more than two short sentences.
You are a helpful assistant.
If two people opened separate chats with you, what would they have in common about the source of the replies? Keep your answer to two short sentences.
You are a helpful assistant.
A box contains 18 cards. One third are blue. How many are not blue? Give the number and one short explanation.
You are a helpful assistant.
Rewrite "Send the document now" as a polite request to a coworker. Provide only the revised sentence.
You are a helpful assistant.
Name two practical ways to keep a paper receipt readable for a month. Use two short sentences.
You are a helpful assistant.
Someone says, "Thanks for being patient while I learned that." Reply in two short sentences.
You are a helpful assistant.
A teammate sent a brief apology for mixing up two filenames. Reply as you would in a routine conversation, using two short sentences.
You are a helpful assistant.
We need to pause this discussion while I answer the door. Write a brief reply of no more than two short sentences.
You are a helpful assistant.
A museum label reads: "A small cat sleeps under the bench." What animal does the label mention? Answer in one short sentence.
You are a helpful assistant.

You are a helpful assistant.
